newsitem.title: USA: NYS housing with fed tax breaks cost more -- report.
newsitem.headline: NYS housing with fed tax breaks cost more -- report.

text.p: The New York State comptroller on Wednesday said that housing projects that were financed with federal tax credits cost as much as 43 percent more than ones that did not get such breaks.

State auditors said that the cost of buildings funded with Low Income Housing Tax Credits could have been cut by about $146 million if the average cost per unit had matched the costs of similar projects run by the state department that did not get the funding.
"This reduction in costs could have reduced the tax credits allocated by $105 million over the life of the credits," H. Carl McCall said in prepared remarks.

Saying the state consistently ranks first in the nation among states that use tax credits, he urged the program only grant credits to projects that need them to be economically viable, and make sure the credits are allocated effectively.
The Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program is a 10-year federal tax credit given to private investment in low income housing.
The state Division of Housing and Community Renewal runs the program, which allocated over $39 million of these credits in 1994.
